top_stories.title: Anthropic releases Claude Haiku 5.5 at steep price cut
points: Priced at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens for requests up to 100,000 tokens (a token limit measuring how much text the model processes at once)\u2014about 90% cheaper than Haiku 4.5.
This matches OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna pricing for smaller workloads, but above 100,000 tokens output pricing jumps 5x, making Haiku less competitive for large-context tasks.
Haiku 5.5's tokenizer counts roughly 1.25x more tokens than Haiku 4.5 for the same text, partially offsetting the advertised savings.
Supports adjustable reasoning effort (a mode where the model spends more or less time 'thinking' before responding), defaulting to medium, with low/medium/high options.
Claude's Python and TypeScript SDKs now support computer and browser automation in beta, removing the need to manually code automation loops.
Image/drawing generation quality improved significantly; one complex test task cost just over 3 cents to run.

unique_angles.point: Reports Haiku shows higher benchmark scores than GPT-6 Luna for workloads under the 100,000-token threshold.
Built for 'sub-agent' work (smaller AI helper tasks within a larger system) and integrates directly into automation workflows.

top_stories.title: Grok Bot routes tasks to rival AI models
points: Elon Musk's Grok Bot now automatically routes work to outside AI services\u2014Claude Opus 5.5 for reasoning, Midjourney for images, and Suno for music\u2014picking the best provider per task.
Users cannot manually select which model handles a request; Grok Bot decides automatically, though usage logs show which model was used.
Billing follows whichever model actually performs the work, and early users report zero API costs for X (formerly Twitter) search and monitoring without needing extra connectors.
Enterprise customers can set an allowlist of approved models, but Grok Bot warns it may not always honor the list; no published data yet proves the routing actually improves results.

unique_angles.point: Highlighted as a surprising strategic move since SpaceX/xAI competes directly with the AI labs whose models it's now routing to.

items.title: OpenAI's unreadable 'mathpocalypse' proofs
points: OpenAI released 372 mathematical proofs claimed as breakthroughs, but the writing is so poor that human experts cannot verify them without AI-assisted translation.
Citations within the papers are frequently irrelevant or confusing, raising doubts about the proofs' actual rigor and validity.
No human has yet confirmed understanding of any of the proofs, highlighting a gap between AI-generated research output and human-readable documentation.

items.title: Zuckerberg's Biohub launches $1.8B biological data initiative
points: Biohub (a Zuckerberg-cofounded nonprofit) is partnering with the DOE and NIH to build standardized, AI-ready biological datasets for disease research.
DOE is committing over $500 million over five years for lab measurement, modeling, and computation infrastructure; NIH will coordinate dataset contributions from existing repositories.
Goal is to give AI models structured training data to help discover new disease prevention and treatment methods.

items.title: First nuclear clocks built in Vienna and Beijing
points: New nuclear clocks lose only about one second every few million years, offering extreme timekeeping precision.
They could potentially detect dark matter particles by measuring subtle wobbles in thorium atomic nuclei.

items.title: Open-source AI clones threaten Adobe's Creative Suite
points: Developer Artcraft released early alpha open-source tools recreating Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat Pro.
Built using Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic's most capable language model); still 'super early alpha' but developer projects 99% feature parity within months.
Could disrupt Adobe's subscription-based business model if full feature parity is reached at zero cost to users.

items.title: Google Playground turns text prompts into playable games
points: Lets teams describe a 2D or 3D game in natural language, then tweak physics, rules, and mechanics in real time without writing code.
Enables quick validation of game concepts before committing full engineering resources.
Planned Unity Spark integration will convert browser prototypes into production-ready Unity builds.
Currently live for U.S. users, with AI-generated games playable directly in-browser.

items.title: A practical framework for building reliable AI evals
points: One successful AI output proves nothing; reliable systems need repeatable tests against known-good answers scored with error margins.
Cheap automated checks (like code linters) catch obvious errors but miss subtler semantic mistakes; AI 'judge' models can catch more but need their own validation.
Roughly 60+ test cases are needed to reliably detect a 12+ percentage point difference in performance.
Production systems should use clear release thresholds and ongoing monitoring rather than relying on public benchmarks, which shift over time and with setup.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 for all users
points: New 'intelligent UI' builds interactive diagrams and comparisons progressively as it generates them, rather than waiting for the full response.
Improved judgment on when to search the web versus rely on trained knowledge, boosting accuracy for time-sensitive questions.
Strengthened safety training resists multi-turn attacks (attempts to bypass safety rules across several conversation turns) involving cyberattacks, bio-threats, and violence.

items.title: Samsung forecasts record $80 billion quarterly profit
points: Projected 107 trillion won (~$80 billion) operating profit marks a fourth consecutive record quarter\u2014the highest ever for any tech company.
Profit surged nine-fold year-over-year, driven by AI-fueled demand pushing up prices for DRAM, NAND flash, and high-bandwidth memory (specialized memory chips used in AI processing).
Chip division drove most gains, while the smartphone unit struggled as higher component costs squeezed profitability.

items.title: AI threatens to crack crypto wallet encryption
points: Ethereum researcher Justin Drake warns AI could break ECDSA (the cryptographic algorithm securing crypto wallets) within months rather than years.
Cites recent AI math breakthroughs, including 10,000 AI agents reportedly solving the Navier-Stokes equation in 88 hours, as evidence attackers could recover private keys sooner than expected.
Advises large crypto holders to move funds to fresh addresses now, while cautioning that a hasty mass migration could itself cause problems.

items.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini agent for enterprise
points: New AI agent connects to business systems and delivers results directly into documents, email, and developer tools employees already use.
